title: Bernoulli factors of group shifts
exact_target: Does every nonabelian group shift have an equal-entropy Bernoulli factor through a continuous group homomorphism?
definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
Let $G$ be a finite group, $d\ge1$, and $X\le G^{\mathbb Z^d}$ a closed
subgroup invariant under all shifts $(\sigma^v x)_u=x_{u+v}$. Equip $X$
with the product topology and normalized Haar measure. This is a group
shift; no commutativity assumption is imposed on $G$ or $X$.
A Bernoulli group shift is $H^{\mathbb Z^d}$ with its shift action,
where $H$ is a finite group.

An algebraic factor map is a continuous surjective group homomorphism
$\pi:X\to H^{\mathbb Z^d}$ satisfying
$\pi\sigma^v=\sigma^v\pi$ for every $v$. The substantive source question
asks whether every nonabelian group shift has such a factor of equal
entropy:
\[
 h_{\rm top}(X)=\log|H|.
\]
Here entropy is the asymptotic logarithmic growth of allowed patterns
per lattice site, computed on increasingly large cubes. The full group
shift on $H$ has entropy $\log|H|$.

The equal-entropy requirement is supplied by the original
Boyle–Schraudner results underlying the survey. Without it the map to
the one-element group would make the literal existence question
vacuous. Their theorem already gives an equal-entropy topological
Bernoulli factor for every group shift, and an algebraic such factor
in the abelian case. The target is therefore to preserve multiplication
in the nonabelian case. Neither a merely measurable factor nor a
continuous factor that fails to be a homomorphism meets that requirement.

\subsection{Short English statement}
Does every nonabelian group shift have an equal-entropy Bernoulli factor through a continuous group homomorphism?
